title: Placement policy serialization and activation guide
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc collects notes and a working proposal for how placement / routing policies are serialized into the control-plane, validated, and safely activated across multi-region deployments. Focus is on: compact wire format, forward/backwards compatibility, server-side validation policy, and a staged activation workflow for live traffic (canaries, metrics gating, automated rollback).

Audience:
Platform engineers, release engineers, and SREs owning control-plane rollouts and policy authoring tooling.

Goals (high level):
- Define a stable JSON/YAML serialization for placement policies that is compact yet expressive enough for region-/capacity-aware routing.
- Provide a validator/linter checklist for pre-flight checks and CI gating.
- Prescribe a rollout activation plan (canary matrix, SLO/metric gates, rollback criteria).
- Capture backwards compatibility rules and migration steps for policy schema upgrades.

Design constraints and principles:
- Wire-compact: policies are frequently updated; avoid fields that duplicate runtime defaults.
- Explicit intent: policy authors should be able to specify preferred region, hard constraints (must/satisfy), and graded preferences (soft weights).
- Versioned schema: every serialized payload carries a top-level "schema_version" string so we can evolve safely.

(this key is only used to break long body strings in the file—final ingestion will concatenate)

Minimal example (JSON) - v1.0:
---
{
  "schema_version": "placement.v1",
  "id": "policy-ml-hot-2026-02",
  "selector": {
    "service_name": "text-generation",
    "route_tags": ["low-latency", "customer-A"]
  },
  "placement": {
    "primary": { "regions": ["us-west1", "us-east1"], "min_capacity": 2 },
    "secondary": { "regions": ["europe-west2"], "min_capacity": 1, "weight": 0.1 },
    "fallback": { "region": "global", "weight": 0.0 }
  },
  "constraints": [
    { "type": "hardware", "operator": "in", "values": ["t4", "a10g"] },
    { "type": "latency_ms", "operator": "<=", "value": 200 }
  ],
  "activation": { "default_mode": "staged", "canary": { "traffic_percent": 5, "duration_minutes": 30 } },
  "metadata": { "author": "maya.chen@redwood.ai", "notes": "quantized variant only" }
}
---
Notes on fields:
- selector: exact+tag based targeting for which routes this policy applies to. Keep selectors conservative (avoid empty selectors).
- placement.primary / secondary: ordered preference, runtime will attempt primary set then score secondary. Weight is used by smart-router to balance during partial activation.
- constraints: allow runtime and validator to early-fail clearly unsatisfiable policies (e.g., require gpu that doesn't exist in region).
- activation: lightweight activation metadata to guide control-plane when enabling. We want a model where policy author can suggest a canary, but activation controller enforces account quotas and safety buckets.

Validation checklist (CI + control-plane preflight):
- schema_version present and recognized by validator; unknown versions reject (soft reject with guidance).
- selector non-empty and resolves to at least one active route in metadata index (unless explicitly marked as draft).
- no contradictory constraints (e.g., region=eu + hardware=only-ashburn-region-hosted).
- aggregate min_capacity does not exceed account reserved capacity for target regions.
- weight values sum sanity check when used in fractional balancing (tolerate small rounding errors <0.01).
- no usage of deprecated capability flags (validator has a deprecation table).
- activation.canary traffic_percent between 0.1 and 50.0 for staged activations; if >20, require explicit approval tag.
- all referenced model variants/quantization profiles must exist in the model catalog at specified versions.

Validator output model (what CI shows):
- PASS/FAIL with line-numbered hints (human readable).
- auto-suggests fixes (e.g., replace region eu-central1 -> europe-west2 if hardware mismatch).
- Risk score (0-100) computed from constraints strictness, min_capacity pressure, and activation aggressiveness.

Rollout/activation mechanics (recommended):
1) Author pushes policy into control-plane as "pending" with activation.default_mode=staged.
2) Preflight runs validator; if PASS -> move to staging namespace (no traffic).
3) Staging runs topology simulation (control-plane sim), generating expected traffic steering matrix and predicted cost delta.
4) If simulation passes (no hard constraint violations), leader invokes canary activation: apply to a small % (activation.canary.traffic_percent).
5) Metrics gating (observed during canary): p50 latency, p95 latency, error_rate, successful_call_ratio, per-token unit_cost, embedding-quality-regression (if applicable).
   - Gate thresholds: p95 increase > 25% => fail; error_rate increase > 1% absolute => fail; unit_cost increase > 30% with no quality improvement => manual review.
6) If canary stable for activation.canary.duration_minutes, increment traffic in exponential steps (5% -> 15% -> 35% -> 100%), re-check gates at each step.
7) On breach: automatic rollback to previous policy version (control-plane stores last-known-good manifest). Escalation to on-call if rollback fails.

Automation hooks and sanity nets:
- Each policy change must have an associated change-id (git SHA or change ticket) to allow fast correlation in logs.
- Control-plane keeps a versioned timeline. Activation operations are idempotent and approach convergent semantics (re-apply -> no-op).
- Telemetry: route-level traces annotated with policy_id and activation_version to analyze regressions.

Compatibility and versioning rules:
- Additive fields allowed; removal or rename requires a migration step and bump of schema_version.
- Runtime ignores unknown optional fields (forward-compatibility) but validator warns if those fields are unknown by the current schema parser.
- If an older runtime encounters a newer schema_version, control-plane must reject activation and route to a safety fallback (default policy) with an audible alert.

Edge cases and open questions (notes to self):
- How to represent per-customer soft-affinity when multiple policies match the same selector? Priority and tie-breaker semantics need a compact precedence field.
- Should placement payloads include explicit "cost_estimate" to speed sim? Tradeoff: stale estimates vs convenience.
- Can we compress repeated region lists via region-groups (e.g., WEST_US) to reduce payload size? Backwards-compatibility concern.
- Document needs a CRUD lifecycle: authoring UI, CLI authoring helpers, and automated migration tooling.

Lint rules to implement in validator service (short):
- pref: no absolute region names if region-group exists for account; warn otherwise.
- pref: authors must set metadata.notes for experimental policies.
- hard: constraints operator must be one of allowed set (in, not_in, <=, >=, ==).
- hard: min_capacity must be integer >=0.
- hard: activation.{canary.duration_minutes, traffic_percent} present for staged activations.

Testing and QA recommendations:
- unit tests: serializer round-trip (serialize->deserialize->compare), validator fuzz tests with synthetic region/hardware inventories.
- sim tests: run per-tenant simulation for 1000 synthetic requests and verify steady-state distribution matches weights within 5%.
- integration: stage the policy in a non-prod control-plane connected to a canary-serving fleet to validate end-to-end.

Operational runbook (brief):
- If rollouts spike errors: abort activation, rollback via control-plane UI (button) or CLI (cpctl rollback <policy_id>), alert on-call.
- If rollback fails: isolate traffic to global-fallback policy and escalate to platform-engineering incident.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Finalize schema fields for v1.1 (priority and precedence). Owner: Ethan. Due: 2026-03-01.
- [ ] Implement validator rule set and deprecation table. Owner: Sofia. Due: 2026-03-10.
- [ ] Add region-group compression to serializer RFC; evaluate storage impact. Owner: Ravi. Due: 2026-03-15.

References and related docs:
- control-plane-routing-playbook (internal)
- telemetry/route-annotations-spec
- infra/catalog/model-variants.json

Notes: this is intentionally informal — expect multiple iterations. Keep selectors conservative and prefer staged activations for anything that touches >1 region.

Last thought: small policies shipped often beat large monolithic policy dumps — encourage smaller, composable placement fragments.
